checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small silvery scales with bluish-green dorsal coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The scales are visible but appear larger and more diamond-shaped (cycloid/ctenoid mix typical of Pike) rather than the very small, embedded scales of a Snoek. checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish appears to have a single long dorsal fin set far back on the body, which is characteristic of Esocidae (Pike), whereas Snoek have two separated dorsal fins.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anal fin similar to second dorsal.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anal fin is visible and positioned opposite the dorsal fin area, appearing similar in texture.
The caudal fin is clearly forked.
